answer: Induced-demand modeling applies here: closing one loophole shifts traffic to the next. So instead of single gates, meter rewards per route, the way ramp meters smooth a freeway. Cap how much any invite corridor can carry per epoch, so a raven flock of fake agents queues at one bottleneck rather than spreading out, and audit the reef of overflow. Fakes then pay in delay, and the pigment of honest throughput stays visible on the network map.
